skill.name: perplexity-search
skill.description: Search current web and research sources with Perplexity models through LiteLLM and OpenRouter. The skill includes CLI scripts, setup guidance, model selection advice, and query strategies for source-grounded answers.
skill.summary: Run Perplexity-backed web research through OpenRouter with guided setup and model selection.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static warnings are documentation examples, placeholders, or Markdown formatting false positives. Confirmed risks involve plaintext API-key handling, user-controlled file writes, shell profile secret storage guidance, and third-party disclosure of search queries through OpenRouter. No evidence found of prompt injection attempts in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.issue: The setup script prints the full API key in an export command.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the key from printed output. Show a placeholder command or instruct users to source the created environment file instead.

remediation.issue: The setup flow accepts API keys through command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer interactive hidden input, existing environment variables, or a documented manual edit flow to reduce shell history and process-list exposure.

remediation.issue: Search queries are sent to OpenRouter and Perplexity through LiteLLM.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy notice and warn users to remove secrets, private research, customer data, and regulated information from queries.

remediation.issue: Output and environment-file paths can overwrite local files.
remediation.suggestion: Check for existing files, require overwrite confirmation, and restrict setup output to safe project-local paths where possible.

remediation.issue: The guide recommends storing API keys in shell startup files.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a project-local ignored .env file, a secret manager, or temporary session exports over persistent shell profile entries.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Query Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The search function sends the full user query to LiteLLM completion for OpenRouter Perplexity models. Users may disclose sensitive internal or unpublished research data to a third-party API when they run searches.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code passes query directly as message content to completion(), and SKILL.md states the skill uses OpenRouter. This is intended behavior, but the privacy exposure is real.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Printed During Setup
semantic_findings.description: The setup script prints an export command containing the user-supplied API key. The key can be exposed in terminal logs, shared screenshots, or captured output.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 157 interpolates args.api_key into output after accepting --api-key. This is a direct local disclosure of a secret.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Accepted on Command Line
semantic_findings.description: The setup flow accepts the OpenRouter key through --api-key. Command-line secrets can appear in shell history and process listings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The parser defines --api-key and later uses args.api_key for setup. This is common, but it is less safe than interactive input or environment-based setup.

high_findings.title: Hidden file in home directory

content.value_statement: Current research changes faster than base model knowledge can track. This skill adds Perplexity-backed search through OpenRouter, with model guidance and citation-focused workflows.
actual_capabilities: Runs a CLI search script that calls Perplexity models through LiteLLM and OpenRouter.
Supports Sonar Pro, Sonar Pro Search, Sonar, Sonar Reasoning Pro, and Sonar Reasoning.
Checks whether LiteLLM and the OpenRouter API key are configured.
Saves successful search answers and usage details to a local output file when requested.
Provides guides for model selection, OpenRouter setup, and effective research query design.
Supports max token, temperature, model, verbose, and setup-check options.
limitations: Requires an OpenRouter API key, account credits, network access, and the LiteLLM package.
Sends search queries to third-party model providers through OpenRouter.
Search quality depends on available web sources and Perplexity model behavior.
Does not independently verify citations or replace expert review for high-stakes decisions.

use_cases.title: Find Recent Scientific Literature
use_cases.description: Locate recent papers, clinical trial updates, and source-grounded summaries for a focused research question.

use_cases.title: Compare Current Technical Options
use_cases.description: Gather current evidence about tools, frameworks, models, or methods before making an engineering decision.

use_cases.title: Verify Time-Sensitive Claims
use_cases.description: Check recent announcements, documentation changes, or policy updates with source-aware web search.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Current Search
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you need a current answer with sources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for the most current information about [topic]. Summarize the answer and include the main sources to verify.

prompt_templates.title: Recent Literature Scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when reviewing a scientific or clinical topic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search recent peer-reviewed work from [time period] about [research question]. Focus on study type, findings, and limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Model-Guided Deep Research
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a question needs multi-step synthesis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the best Perplexity model for a complex comparison of [option A] and [option B]. Include criteria, tradeoffs, and cited evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Structured Evidence Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when preparing a decision brief.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search current sources about [decision topic]. Produce an evidence summary with confidence, disagreements, source quality, and unanswered questions.

output_examples.input: Search for recent CAR-T therapy results in solid tumors.
output_examples.output: A concise evidence summary with trial names, reported outcomes, safety notes, and source citations for follow-up review.

output_examples.input: Compare Sonar Pro and Sonar Pro Search for a literature review.
output_examples.output: A model recommendation explaining quality, cost, speed, and when deeper agentic search is worth the extra expense.

output_examples.input: Find current guidance for implementing Kafka to PostgreSQL streaming.
output_examples.output: A technical summary covering common architectures, backpressure handling, delivery guarantees, and links to current documentation.

best_practices: Use specific queries with time ranges, domain terms, source preferences, and expected output format.
Start with Sonar Pro, then choose cheaper or deeper models based on complexity and budget.
Review cited sources directly before using results in research, product, medical, or legal decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not paste secrets, private data, or unpublished sensitive research into search queries.
Do not treat generated answers as verified facts without checking the cited sources.
Do not use the most expensive model for simple lookups that a basic search can answer.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Perplexity API key?
faq.answer: No. It uses Perplexity models through OpenRouter, so an OpenRouter API key is required.

faq.question: Can it search information newer than the base model cutoff?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is designed for current web-grounded search through Perplexity models.

faq.question: Does it work in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it save results locally?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI can write successful results to a user-specified output file.

faq.question: Is it safe to search private data?
faq.answer: No. Queries are sent to third-party model providers, so sensitive data should be removed first.

faq.question: Which model should I start with?
faq.answer: Start with Sonar Pro for balanced quality and cost, then adjust based on complexity.
